Q: How do table structure, reading order and OCR confidence affect trustworthy extraction?
A:
Character recognition is only one part of document extraction. A table also needs row/column relationships, headers, units and page context.

Reading text in visual coordinate order can still join unrelated columns or detach a value from its label. Confidence scores describe a model's estimate under its contract, not an independently calibrated guarantee of semantic correctness. Preserve page locations and source regions so critical fields can be verified, and route ambiguous high-impact extractions to review instead of silently inventing structure.
Why: A fee table shows different amounts for standard and urgent service. Flattening both columns into one sentence can attach the urgent fee to the standard option despite every character being recognized correctly.
Risk: Good character accuracy can coexist with a wrong business interpretation.
Trade: Layout-aware extraction adds cost but can preserve relationships plain text loses.
Try: Verify a multi-column table using source coordinates and check label/value associations.
